newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Escudo slips but not seen falling far.
newsitem.headline: Escudo slips but not seen falling far.

text.p: The escudo wobbled on Thursday, slipping to close to 101.00 to the German mark from its opening 100.64/67, but analysts said they did not see the currency coming under sustained selling pressure.
It was not clear whether the Bank of Portugal had intervened discreetly when the currency touched a low of 100.94 before it recovered slightly to 100.82/84 in late trade.
Analysts said that the strength of the economy together with the central bank's well-known aversion to sudden currency movements argued against any prolonged retreat against the German currency.

Some traders said that the weakness had been triggered by speculation over the level at which the escudo could join the single currency now that Portugal is increasingly seen as a probable member of the pioneer group to launch the euro in 1999.

Portuguese investment bank Banco Cisf issued a report earlier this week saying that the escudo could eventually sink towards 102.50 to the mark, its mid-point within the currency grid of the European Monetary System (EMS).
It argued that 102.50 would be a logical level at which to convert escudos into the euro, the European Union's planned single currency.

"It is natural that some think that the escudo is going to depreciate more than other currencies, particularly the peseta, which is already near its (EMS) parity (85.07)," said one foreign exchange trader.
But analysts said the notion that the EMS mid-point could be used was just one possibility amongst several.
"Another would be that they were market rates (at the time) or an average rate over a certain period," said Rui Martins dos Santos, chief economist at Banco Portugues de Investimento.
"It is all still open. You cannot speculate on just one scenario. I personally believe they (the entry rates) should be market rates," he said.
Nuno Godinho of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said that he felt the currency was unlikely to go below 101.50 to the mark.

"(Over the next month) I see the escudo at around 100.00 to 100.50 with the maintenance of optimism (over convergence), the positive fundamentals and inflows for the EDP privatisation," said Martim Amaral Neto do Banco ESSI.
The partial privatisation of state electricity concern EDP, which will be the largest state sale ever, is set for next month.
"Interest rates are not in our favour, because in the short-term they are going to fall significantly, but I don't see the convergence (in interest) rates really hurting the currency,", said Godinho.
Besides the EDP privatisation, Godinho said that there would be inflows of funds from investors seeking to profit from the narrowing of the yield gap with the German Bunds.
In any case, analysts said that they doubted that the Bank of Portugal, with its powerful reserves, would allow the currency to sink to the extent that it could become a threat to inflation targets.
"I believe that the Bank has no interest at all in a depreciation and I think that between 101.00 and 101.25, it would intervene in a more active way," said Amaral Neto.
